text: Databases are organised systems for storing and managing information. In relational databases, data is kept in tables with rows and columns, and SQL is used to write queries that retrieve or change data. NoSQL databases, on the other hand, are more flexible and store data in documents or key-value pairs, which suits large or rapidly changing data. Data modelling helps you plan the structure before you build it, so the database fits your needs. Indexes make queries faster by helping the database find data quickly. Choosing the right type, structure, and indexes is important for good performance.
